title: Watched Pot
intro: The long slab is a rotator: it turns the polarization steadily, so a horizontal packet leaves it vertical and the horizontal exit polarizer blocks it. Watch it on the way: each polarizer you insert projects the polarization back to horizontal, losing only sin² of the small angle turned since the last one. Many frequent looks freeze the rotation (the quantum Zeno effect, as in Kwiat's interaction-free measurement). How you space them matters.
goal: Place up to five horizontal polarizers inside the rotator so the packet stays horizontal and passes the exit polarizer into the target.

physics.point: Check a slowly turning polarization often and it hardly turns. Each polarizer resets it to horizontal at a small cost, so many evenly spaced looks freeze the rotation.

idea: The slab turns the polarization at a steady rate. The packet spends 6.4 time units inside and comes out vertical, turned by 90°. The exit polarizer is horizontal, so it blocks.

A horizontal polarizer inside the slab asks: still horizontal? After a small turn α the answer is 'yes' with probability cos²α, and a 'yes' sets the polarization back to exactly horizontal. The turning starts again from zero.
Small turns cost very little, because cos²α ≈ 1 − α² for small α. Cut the 90° into many small steps and the total loss shrinks. Watching often freezes the evolution: the quantum Zeno effect.
Spacing matters. Equal spacing gives equal small steps. Bunched polarizers leave large turns between the bunches, and large turns are expensive.

With n polarizers equally spaced, the 90° is cut into N = n + 1 steps, and there are N looks (n polarizers plus the exit):
For large N, P ≈ 1 − π²/(4N), which tends to 1.

Measured as a share of what reaches the target without the rotator (37%): 0.24, 0.42, 0.55, 0.63, 0.69 for 1 to 5 polarizers. They sit a little above the ideal law because each polarizer is 1 unit thick and keeps watching while the slab turns inside it. Five bunched in the middle give 0.50.
try: Place one polarizer at the slab's centre (x = 19): P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 9%. Add more, evenly spaced, and watch P<sub>T</sub> grow.
Space all five evenly (x ≈ 13.7, 16.3, 19, 21.7, 24.3): P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 26%. Push them together in the middle: about 19%.
Put all five near the slab's far end: the polarization has already turned most of the way, and P<sub>T</sub> falls to about 3%.
